### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **50** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 447226b222467709ed74ca99eaf808c178656b33`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/rest/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/meta/:type (route, 40 pages)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **181** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 447226b222467709ed74ca99eaf808c178656b33` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f177a461b7327709169153c9f694cc019e136979` — the merge of head `621212ae86bbac8cb5f6a5a434b8a9c9e2dae120` into base `447226b222467709ed74ca99eaf808c178656b33`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f177a461b7327709169153c9f694cc019e136979 && git checkout f177a461b7327709169153c9f694cc019e136979
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 447226b222467709ed74ca99eaf808c178656b33 621212ae86bbac8cb5f6a5a434b8a9c9e2dae120 && git checkout -B drift-repro 447226b222467709ed74ca99eaf808c178656b33 && git merge --no-ff 621212ae86bbac8cb5f6a5a434b8a9c9e2dae120

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 447226b222467709ed74ca99eaf808c178656b33
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 447226b222467709ed74ca99eaf808c178656b33` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5f55d49c574d697676d4c93a0a95fbc72d17675f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` + `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.test.ts` (the describe and the deleted marker pin), `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` (`META_LIST_QUERY_PARAMS`, `metaListQueryRefusal`, `metaListUnknownParamRefusal`, `metaListNames`, chain step 2a, `META_QUERY_ARITY_DOORS.list`), `packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts` (the list door), `packages/rest/src/index.ts` (three new exports), `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` (the dispatcher twin), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` + `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` (the push-down), `packages/client/src/index.ts` (`meta.getItems({ names })`, both surfaces), the six test files beside them, `.changeset/29236-meta-list-names-filter.md`, `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`, `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` (generated); read for the judgments, unchanged on `main`: `packages/rest/src/query-allowlist.ts` (`unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage`, the ingress policy), `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` (`extractLocale`), `metaRequestLocale` and `META_ITEM_READ_PARAMS` in the gate file, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (`readArmToken`), `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (the level axis), `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (`CATEGORIES`), `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (the `package` item shape).

Inputs read: card #29236 body and all 19 comments (triage 6575623583; the measurement 6576480506; the decision 6579872432; the ruling 6580261740, letter A, quoted here as written; seat 5's execution 6580443235 and release 6591626191; the spec seat's inherited items 6594515725 and the blocker landing 6595098031; seat 3's claim 6670429730 with amendments 6670501210, 6671057079 and the re-posted claim 6671541845; os-dev report 6672708990); PR #30709 title, body, 19-file list and net diff vs `main` (merge-base `4bf9a2d7`, 3 ahead; `origin/main` is `f2ea1931`, 20 commits past the merge-base at read time, mergeability unknown); the docs-drift comment 6671701513; follow-up cards #30710 and #29444; the seat's dispatch order; the 65 check-runs on this head; the code cited above on `main` at the merge-base.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The ruling's seven binding sentences, each against the code.** (a) `?names=a,b,c` on every `/meta/:type` list as one comma-separated value: `metaListNames` reads `query.names` as one string, splits on `,`, trims, drops blanks, folds repeats (the data routes' own `fields` / `searchFields` shape, `data-action-routes.ts`), and both transports call it; TRUE. (b) The narrowing runs after the per-caller gate and before the object mask and translation: step 2a of `createMetaListAnswer` sits between the gate (step 1) and the `app` `?id=` step 3, ahead of the mask and `translateMetaList`; the pin records the masker being asked for the named items only, and a withheld `app` named in the filter stays withheld; TRUE. (c) An empty value is refused `400` like `?id=`: `metaListNames` throws `status 400 / VALIDATION_ERROR / param names` on `''`, `','` and `' , '`, caught by `handleRouteError` on REST and `errorFromThrown(e, 400)` on the dispatcher, before any store read (pinned: `getMetaItems` never called); TRUE. (d) An unknown name is simply absent, no 404: a `Set` filter on both the chain and the store read, `200 []` when none match; TRUE. (e) Pushed down to the store read as `GetMetaItemsRequest.names`: `readFlattenedMetaItems` filters once every source is merged and unseated rows are dropped, before the env-wide join, the `package` writable decoration, lock selection, governance and the artifact envelope; the "served exactly as the whole list serves it" pin holds equality; TRUE. (f) The closed set with the `refuseUnknownQueryParams` pattern: `metaListUnknownParamRefusal` asks `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage` (the same sentence `refuseUnknownQueryParams` writes) before `refuseRepeatedQueryParams`, on both transports, so recognition precedes arity as AGENTS.md's rule 5 orders; TRUE. (g) `?id=` keeps its one-app meaning: untouched; TRUE.
- **The closed set is measured, not copied.** I re-measured the list path's read points on `main` at the merge-base: the handler reads `package` (`metaItemPackageBinding`), `preview`, and hands `req.query` to the chain, which reads `id` (app), `object` (view), `include` (doc content, position grants), and `locale` through `requestLocale` → `metaRequestLocale`, which reads `http.query.locale` after `Accept-Language` for every translated list answer and the doc locale collapse. No middleware reads the query on this path. So the set is exactly `package, preview, object, include, id, names, locale`, and the parity census now derives the read set from `meta-collection-routes.ts` plus `createMetaListAnswer` / `metaRequestLocale` / `translateMetaList` / `metaListNames` and pins `META_LIST_QUERY_PARAMS` equal to it, so a seventh-plus read cannot land unlisted.
- **The `locale` deviation is sound, and under AGENTS.md it is required.** Route & surface ownership rule 5 names this exact case: "a parameter such as the export route's `?locale=` is read a frame down (`extractLocale`), never in the handler body", and orders the set measured from the read points, "never from the docs or the card". The item read's `META_ITEM_READ_PARAMS` already carries `locale` for the same reason. A six-member set would turn every `?locale=zh-CN` list read, which answers `200` today, into a `400`, which is the "loud outage" the rule warns against. The ruling's six is a list of the filters; it neither names nor denies `locale`. The PR pins `?locale=zh-CN` `200` on both transports and the ablation "`locale` dropped from the set" goes red (3). Presenting it to the maintainer as a veto point in the PR's 速读 is the right form.
- **Bracketed spellings.** `package[` on every type, `id[` on `app` and `object[` on `view` keep the located sentences the arity step and the chain already answer; every other bracketed key (`names[]`, `id[]` on a non-app type, `object[]` on a non-view type) is an undeclared name and is refused by recognition. The two `meta-app-publish-gate.test.ts` controls that flipped `200 → 400` are exactly these; the flip is the closed set working, not a regression.
- **Consumer census (mine, on `main` at the merge-base).** Producers of `/meta/:type` list query strings: `ui/**` sends only `client.meta.getItems(type)` / `(type, { packageId })`, `GET /meta/view?object=`, `GET /meta/object?package=…&preview=draft`, `GET /meta/position?include=grants` (the `_drafts` and `diagnostics` doors are other routes); `skills/**`, `content/docs/**` outside `references/` and `releases/`, `examples/**`, `packages/{qa,dogfood,cli,mcp,verify,client}` send no key outside the seven. No real caller starts getting `400`; the dispatch order's fork condition is not met. `Test UI` 16/16 and the dogfood battery are green at this head.
- **`packages/spec/src/**` exports and `.describe()` text.** No export is added, removed or renamed in the spec; `check:api-surface` has nothing to move and the file list carries no `api-surface/` or `authorable-surface/` change. The one `.describe()` that changes, `GetMetaItemsRequestSchema.names`, now states: "only the named items of the type are answered, among those the list would answer without it" (TRUE, (b) and (e)); "Sent over HTTP as one comma-separated value (`?names=a,b,c`)" (TRUE, (a); the client joins with `,`); "A name that matches no item is simply absent from the answer (no 404)" (TRUE, (d)); "An empty value is refused with 400 rather than read as every item; leave the key out to list every item" (TRUE, (c); absent `names` sends no filter and the store receives no `names` member, pinned). The `.min(1)` on the array stays and no transport can produce an empty array (the empty string is refused ahead of it). `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` carries the regenerated row and nothing else in the generated tree names the marker for `names`. Declaration equals enforcement; retiring the `[PLANNED — not yet served]` prefix, the trailing sentence and the marker `it(...)` is exactly what 6594515725 asked.
- **Three new `@objectstack/rest` exports** (`META_LIST_QUERY_PARAMS`, `metaListQueryRefusal`, `metaListNames`): the widening half, needed by the dispatcher twin; declared in the PR body and the changeset. `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage` was already exported on `main`, so the runtime test's import resolves.
- **Dispatcher parity.** The twin asks `metaListQueryRefusal(listType, query)` before any read, refuses the unknown type, reads `names` once (empty → `400`), pushes it to `protocol.getMetaItems`, and the metadata-service and registry exits that take no `names` are still narrowed by the chain inside `answerMetaList`. The census's five new probes and the `META_LIST_QUERY_PARAMS == derived.params` pin cover both transports.
- **`package` list items carry no `name`** (`InstalledPackageSchema`, keyed by `manifest.id` / `id`), so `?names=` on `/meta/package` always answers `200 []`. Deviation 5 notes it and changes nothing; see should-fix below.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/29236-meta-list-names-filter.md`: `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/spec`, each `patch`; body opens `feat(rest)!: …`, carries `Clause-②: yes (narrowing + widening) — …` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, a `**BREAKING**` section with Before / Now / Who moves / Remedy, and one `<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) … -->` marker, a member of `CATEGORIES`. The PR body carries the same two lines, and the title carries `!`.

- **Level.** `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: `names` is an API query key, not a key a metadata author writes; the spec change is description text on an already-declared member (added by #29722 as `added`), and no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard moves. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: the level follows the kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". `check-changeset-no-major` enforces the same ("a declared `none` must grade every entry it introduces `patch`"), so deviation 2 (patch, not the ruling's sketched minor) is the rule and the gate, not a choice; the ruling's own `Metadata-protocol: none` already implies it.
- **The narrowing is declared and pinned.** The arm: `readArmToken` takes the first token inside the parenthetical, so `yes (narrowing + widening)` reads as value `yes`, arm `narrowing`, the documented "widens one surface and narrows another" shape; `check-adr-0087-registration` therefore asks for the banner and the disposition, and both are present. Title `!`, BREAKING section with migration (drop the key, or spell it as one of the seven), docs paragraph naming the closed set, and the refusal pinned on both transports with the store never called. Complete.
- Check-runs on `5f55d49c`: 65 runs read, every one `completed`; 57 `success`, 8 `skipped` (`Lint UI`, `UI Published Artifacts`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the opt-in tarball and 18.x harnesses, the live-PG temporal conformance, the sharded dogfood matrix label, the schedule gate), none `in_progress`, none failed. `Check Changeset`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI (1–16/16)`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Docs` all `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none. Deviations 1–5 judged: 1 (`locale`) sound and required, see ①; 2 (patch) sound, see ②; 3 (the `http-protocol.mdx` paragraph) the seat added it to the claim 6671057079 before the PR, in scope; 4 (two controls flipped) correct, see ①; 5 (`package` list) honest but unfiled, should-fix below.
- `Skills-docs:` the PR body still reads `follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md`; the report names #30710. The seat rewrites the body line to `Skills-docs: follow-up #30710` before ACCEPT (pm-dispatch claim template). The deferral itself is honest: the skill today names only declared keys (`?preview=draft`, `?package=`, `?include=content`), so no skill reader is broken by this PR; it merely does not yet teach `?names=`. #30710 is Tier H (`skills/**`), p3, serial after this PR.
- #29444 (ui follow-up) is the consumer's adoption of the new key, Blocked-by this card; nothing a consumer needs now is deferred into it: the client SDK ships `{ names }` in this PR.
- The dev's `Local-runs`-class statements (106 gate families, ablations, dogfood) are not relied on here; the check-runs and the diff are.
- Author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no out-of-relay login. The PR is a draft. `origin/main` moved 20 commits past the merge-base at read time; the landing merges `main` and rebuilds (Multi-agent discipline §10), no contract effect.
- Independence: rendered by an isolated contract-review subagent fed the card, the PR, the diff, the cited code on `main`, the gates' sources and the check-runs, not the seat's or the dev's conclusions; adopted by the seat named in `Reviewed-by:`.

### ④ Design judgment

- `protocol.zod.ts` — the describe states only what both transports now do; the first consumer (the Console roster gate, #29444) reads exactly the sentences a client needs (one value, absent unknowns, empty refused). Holds.
- `meta-item-read-gate.ts` — one decision (`metaListQueryRefusal`) for both transports, recognition before arity, the three bracketed exceptions enumerated by the type whose step reads them, the chain step placed where the ruling put it, and the census pinning the set to the source. The design is the one AGENTS.md rule 5 prescribes and the sibling item read already uses. Holds.
- `protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` — the filter sits after the merge and before every per-item decoration, so the saving the ruling wanted (filter before decorating) is real and the per-item verdicts are unchanged. Holds.
- `client/src/index.ts` — `names !== undefined` sends `?names=` for an empty array, which the server refuses; the docblock says so. Deliberately not dropped into "every item". Holds.
- The narrowing is a breaking change the maintainer ordered; its remedy is one of the seven names; no alias or lenient fallback is added anywhere. Holds.

Findings (none must-fix):

- **should-fix** — `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`, the TSDoc paragraph "**Declared ahead of its producer.** No list door reads `names` yet, so its describe opens `[PLANNED — not yet served]`; the server PR on #29236 drops the marker in the change that serves the member (the pin is in `protocol.test.ts`)." is false on this head: this PR drops the marker and deletes that pin. Rewrite it to say the member is served, or delete the paragraph. Not in the published JSON Schema, so not must-fix, but it is the one false sentence left in the hit file.
- **should-fix** — `?names=` on `GET /meta/package` can never match (deviation 5): `package` items carry `manifest.id` / `id`, no `name`, so a caller gets `200 []`, the silent-zero shape the closed set exists to remove, while the describe and the docs say "every type". Either refuse `?names=` on the `package` list with a located `400`, or match packages by their id, or the seat files a card before ACCEPT (Prime Directive 10: a declared≠enforced trap is an issue, not a note).
- **should-fix** (seat, before ACCEPT) — rewrite the PR body's `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md` to `Skills-docs: follow-up #30710`.
- **nit** — `Clause-②: yes (narrowing + widening)`: the parser reads the arm `narrowing` and treats `+ widening` as trailing reasoning, and `yes` already says widening; the canonical spelling is `yes (narrowing)`.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-ibfnsp`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cytQjG9X1CrCgytUM5`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `621212ae86bbac8cb5f6a5a434b8a9c9e2dae120`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` (`metaListUnknownParamRefusal`, `NAMES_ON_PACKAGE_LIST_MESSAGE`, `MetaItemQueryRefusal.rule`), `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` (the `GetMetaItemsRequestSchema` TSDoc and the `names` describe), `packages/rest/src/meta-query-arity-doors.test.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/dispatcher-query-arity.test.ts`, `.changeset/29236-meta-list-names-filter.md`, `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`, `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` (generated); read for the judgments, unchanged by the delta: `packages/rest/src/index.ts`, `packages/rest/src/meta-collection-routes.ts` and `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts` (the two call sites), `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` (`metaTypeSingular`), `packages/spec/src/meta-spelling/metadata-url-spelling.ts` + `meta-url-data.generated.ts` (`unrecognisedMetaTypeRefusal`, `canonicalMetaUrlType`), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` (the `package` branch), the PR body on this head.

Delta review of record 6672872746 (PASS on `5f55d49c`): exactly one commit, `621212ae` "fix(rest): refuse ?names= on the package list, whose items are keyed by id; retire the stale TSDoc paragraph", parent `5f55d49c`, 7 files, +74/-13 (net vs merge-base `4bf9a2d7`: still 19 files, +850/-49). Nothing else moved: the three new `@objectstack/rest` exports, `META_LIST_QUERY_PARAMS`, the chain step, the push-down, the client and the census are byte-identical to the reviewed head, and that record's judgments stand. The commit folds in the three should-fix items and the nit of 6672872746 under the seat's ruling for a located `400` on the `package` list rather than matching by id.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The new refusal is honest.** On `main` a `package` list item is `InstalledPackageSchema` (keyed by `manifest.id` / `id`, no `name`), so `?names=` there could only answer `200 []` for every value. `metaListUnknownParamRefusal` now answers `{ status: 400, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: NAMES_ON_PACKAGE_LIST_MESSAGE, rule: 'names-on-package' }` when `metaType === 'package'` and the query owns a `names` key, whatever its value (`'crm'`, `''`, an array), pinned for all four spellings. It sits where the closed-set refusal sits, inside the one decision both transports ask: `RestServer`'s door calls `metaListUnknownParamRefusal(listType, req.query)` and the dispatcher calls `metaListQueryRefusal(listType, query)`, which delegates to it first, so the refusal runs on both transports before the arity check, before `refuseUnknownMetaListType` and before any protocol read (pinned on both: `getMetaItems` never called). Same code (`VALIDATION_ERROR`), same nested envelope (REST writes `{ error: { code, message } }`, the dispatcher `queryRefusalAnswer`), same status.
- **Ordering versus the unknown-key refusal is right.** Recognition still outranks it: `{ names: 'crm', zeta: '1' }` on `package` answers the unknown-key sentence for `zeta` (pinned), so a caller fixes the misspelt key first and the located package sentence second, and the arity refusal (`metaQueryArityRefusal('list', …)`) stays after both, as before. `names` stays in `META_LIST_QUERY_PARAMS` (it IS read on every other type), so the parity census's `META_LIST_QUERY_PARAMS == derived.params` pin is undisturbed.
- **Message voice is consistent with its siblings, not with `refuseUnknownQueryParams`, and that is right.** The key is declared, so the "not supported by this endpoint" sentence would be false; the new sentence takes the voice of the list's own per-type refusals (`metaListNames`'s empty refusal, `refuseEmptyListFilter`): what was asked, why it cannot be served ("package items are keyed by id, not by name, so no name could match"), that "The list was not served", and the remedy ("Leave the parameter out to list every package you can see"). No tracker number in the runtime string.
- **Type coverage.** `package` is not a declared URL spelling (`META_URL_TO_SINGULAR` has no entry; `CANONICAL_META_TYPES` lacks it) but a live-registered type that `refuseUnknownMetaListType` admits through `metaTypeIsLive`, and the registry lists it under the singular, so `/meta/package` is the one list spelling that reaches the protocol's `package` branch; `metaType === 'package'` covers it on both transports (`metaTypeSingular` / `pluralToSingular` pass the singular through). The protocol's `request.type === 'packages'` tolerance is an internal branch no admitted list URL reaches.
- **`.describe()` and docblock now true.** The TSDoc paragraph reads "**Served.** Both list doors … read `?names=` and push it down here, on every type except `package` … refuses `?names=` with `400`" — true against the two call sites and the new refusal. The describe adds one sentence, "Served on every type except `package`, whose items are keyed by id; the `package` list refuses it with 400." — true, and every other sentence of the describe is unchanged and was judged TRUE in 6672872746. Declaration equals enforcement for every type now, including the one it formerly over-claimed.
